items.title: Stephen Miller becomes Trump's chief of staff
items.feedTitle: 3 things to know about Stephen Miller, new White House chief of staff
items.summary: President Trump has appointed Stephen Miller, a hardline immigration architect, as his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Miller is known for designing Trump's sweeping immigration crackdown and has been a loyal aide since Trump's 2016 campaign. The move signals Trump's intention to double down on far-right immigration policies despite midterm losses. Critics worry the appointment reflects a shift toward confrontational governance even as the GOP grapples with electoral defeat.

items.title: US homelessness drops significantly after years of record highs
items.feedTitle: Homelessness in the U.S. saw its largest drop in more than a decade last year
items.summary: Homelessness in the US fell substantially last year, marking its largest decline in more than a decade after years of record-high levels. The total remains near 700,000 people, but the drop represents progress on a persistent national crisis. The Trump administration and homeless advocacy groups cite different reasons for the decline, suggesting disagreement over what policies drove the improvement.

items.title: Job growth exceeds expectations despite AI bubble concerns
items.feedTitle: What to know about a better-than-expected jobs report amid AI bubble concerns
items.summary: Employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, better than anticipated, with gains in August and September revised upward by a combined 84,000 jobs. The labor market shows resilience even as questions grow about sustainability of AI investments. The three-month trend suggests the economy remains relatively stable despite broader economic uncertainties.

items.title: Public school enrollment faces massive projected drop nationwide
items.feedTitle: Why public schools nationwide are facing a massive drop in student enrollment
items.summary: School enrollment is expected to plunge by 2 million children by 2030, a trend experts warn will be accelerated by potential mass deportations of immigrant families with school-age children. The crisis threatens educational systems already strained by demographic shifts. Education experts worry the combination of demographic decline and immigration enforcement could severely destabilize district budgets and services.

items.title: Hispanic voters power Democratic wins in midterm elections
items.feedTitle: Hispanic voters were key in powering Democratic midterm wins
items.summary: Hispanic voters were key to Democrats' sweeping midterm victories, with Latino support shifting leftward after Trump had made inroads with some Hispanic constituencies. Exit polling showed significant movement among Latino voters back toward Democrats. The voting bloc's decisive role highlights the importance of immigration and economic issues in shaping electoral outcomes.

stlouis.title: SLU defeats Missouri 90-84 in rivalry game
stlouis.feedTitle: SLU rises to the challenge, beats Missouri 90-84 as rivalry gets restarted
stlouis.summary: Saint Louis University's Billikens defeated the University of Missouri Tigers 90-84 in the Show Me Showdown rivalry game on November 6. McCottry and Sharma each scored 17 points for SLU, which made 14 three-pointers to overcome Missouri. The victory marked a successful restart of the intrastate rivalry.

stlouis.title: St. Louis County property tax bills corrected after errors
stlouis.feedTitle: Corrected St. Louis County property tax bills back online after errors, county says
stlouis.summary: Corrected St. Louis County property tax bills have been restored online after errors were identified and fixed by county officials. The county acknowledged the problem and restored access to corrected billing information for residents.

stlouis.title: College transit challenge promotes Metro Transit ridership
stlouis.feedTitle: College transit challenge promotes Metro Transit use for students
stlouis.summary: A college transit challenge initiative is encouraging student use of St. Louis area Metro Transit services. The program aims to promote public transportation adoption among the student population during the academic year.

items.title: Six killed in Kraków mass shooting, suspect had far-right views
items.feedTitle: Six dead after gunman opens fire in Kraków market square, with three more victims found at suspect’s home
items.summary: A gunman opened fire in Kraków's main market square, killing six people and wounding 16 others, with three additional victims found at the suspect's home. Polish authorities identified the 25-year-old suspect as holding far-right ideologies and ultra-nationalistic views. Poland's defense minister called the attack an 'act of terror,' while the prime minister vowed a strong response to the violence.

items.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with government formation
items.feedTitle: Eisenkot chosen over Netanyahu to form Israel’s next government
items.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally asked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, a setback for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu whose coalition lost its majority in last month's election. Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot secured a clear majority, but representatives from most Israeli parties recommended Eisenkot be given the chance to assemble a coalition. Eisenkot has 28 days to secure the required Knesset seats.

items.title: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty after tight election
items.feedTitle: NZ election 2026: New Zealand faces weeks of uncertainty with results ‘too close to call’
items.summary: New Zealand's election results are too close to call, with no party securing a decisive majority. The nation could face weeks of coalition negotiations to determine the shape of the next government. Initial results show a highly divided parliament with both major blocs struggling to gain clear advantage.

items.title: Airstrikes near Yemen's capital kill at least 25 people
items.feedTitle: Houthi-run health ministry says airstrikes kill 33 near Yemen capital
items.summary: At least 25 people were killed and 30 injured in airstrikes near Sanaa, Yemen's capital, according to Houthi officials, with civilian casualties including mostly women and children. The strikes mark some of the deadliest single incidents in the ongoing Yemen conflict. Responsibility and details remain contested between warring parties.

items.title: Canary Islands declare emergency over migrant influx
items.feedTitle: Canary Islands’ El Hierro declares emergency amid migrant, refugee influx
items.summary: Spain's Canary Islands declared an emergency after more than 3,300 migrants and refugees arrived by boat since the start of November. Island officials, particularly El Hierro, are requesting government assistance to manage the unprecedented surge in arrivals. The influx has strained local resources and triggered a humanitarian response from Spanish authorities.

items.title: Tech Mahindra ex-Asia head shot dead over parking dispute
items.feedTitle: Tech Mahindra’s ex-Asia head shot dead over parking row in Faridabad, neighbour arrested
items.summary: A former Tech Mahindra Asia regional head was shot dead in Faridabad over a parking lot disagreement with a neighbor. Police arrested the neighbor after the shooting, which involved multiple gunshots. The incident highlights rising tensions over residential disputes escalating to violence.

items.title: Ayodhya lights up 30 lakh diyas for Deepotsav celebration
items.feedTitle: Ayodhya glows with 30 lakh diyas as Deepotsav lights up Saryu ghats on Diwali eve
items.summary: Ayodhya illuminated over 30 lakh earthen lamps along the Saryu River ghats for the Deepotsav Diwali celebration. The grand festival display drew crowds for the annual religious and cultural observance marking India's most prominent temple city. The event reflects Diwali's continuing importance as a major national celebration.

items.title: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
items.feedTitle: Rajnath Singh warns of evolving threats, calls for highest military readiness
items.summary: Summary unavailable for this update.

items.title: Kerala measles outbreak highlights disease pattern shifts
items.feedTitle: Keralam measles outbreaks call for a relook at disease epidemiology
items.summary: Measles, historically a childhood disease affecting ages one to five, is now spreading across all age groups in Kerala, including among fully vaccinated individuals and infants below vaccination age. The unusual pattern suggests changing epidemiology of the disease. Public health experts are calling for a reassessment of disease surveillance and vaccination strategies.

items.title: Migrant workers return home ahead of Deepavali festival rush
items.feedTitle: Ahead of Deepavali, Chhath festivals, migrants reach Bihar in hordes covering thousands of kilometers
items.summary: Thousands of migrant workers are traveling thousands of kilometers to return home for the Deepavali and Chhath festivals, a seasonal pattern reflecting India's large mobile labor force. Young workers from Bengaluru traveled 2,200 km by auto-rickshaw to reach Bihar. The festival season drives massive population movement across Indian regions.

immigration.title: Democrats' Congress control raises H-1B relief hopes for Indian workers
immigration.feedTitle: Can Democrats reverse Trump's H-1B policies? What US midterms mean for immigrants
immigration.summary: With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress following the midterm sweep, Indian H-1B visa holders and immigration advocates are hopeful that Trump-era restrictions may face scrutiny and possible reversal. Lawyers caution, however, that immediate relief is unlikely given Trump remains president through early 2025. Democratic legislative focus may instead emphasize oversight of H-1B restrictions and trade policies affecting India.

immigration.title: USCIS issues new good moral character guidance for naturalization
immigration.feedTitle: New USCIS guidance on good moral character determination for N-400 application
immigration.summary: USCIS has released new guidance on how to assess 'good moral character' for N-400 naturalization applications (proposed, not final). The memorandum will likely affect citizenship eligibility determinations. This guidance update comes as the administration tightens standards for new citizens, alongside broader changes to immigration enforcement.

immigration.title: Over 1.56 million US green card applications face backlogs
immigration.feedTitle: More than 1.56 million US green card applications face backlog
immigration.summary: USCIS data shows more than 1.56 million green card applications are pending, highlighting severe processing delays in the employment-based immigration system. The backlog affects both Indian and other nationality visa applicants seeking permanent residency (finalized and in effect—data current as of October 2026). Processing delays may exceed several years for some employment categories.

items.title: AI stock selloff wipes trillions after Democrats' midterm sweep
items.feedTitle: How midterm elections sent Wall Street from celebration to mayhem in just 24 hours / this week
items.summary: Wall Street experienced sharp reversals after the midterm elections, with AI-heavy tech stocks suffering a brutal correction that erased nearly $2.5 trillion in market value in a single week. Investors initially celebrated Democratic victories but then began pricing in concerns about stricter AI regulation and data center restrictions. The selloff marks the worst week for the S&P 500 since April 2025's tariff crash.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway accelerates buybacks as profits decline
items.feedTitle: Berkshire Hathaway speeds up stock buybacks, though profit falls
items.summary: Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway more than doubled its stock buyback pace in the third quarter to $377 billion while reported earnings fell. The aggressive share repurchase signals confidence despite profitability headwinds. The move reflects Buffett's long-standing preference for buybacks over acquisitions in a volatile market environment.

items.title: Indian markets surge as Nifty gains 8.58% in best week since 2021
items.feedTitle: NSE sees increased stock market activity as Nifty 50 closes the week up 2.01%
items.summary: India's Sensex gained 8.82% and Nifty 50 surged 8.58% in the week ending November 6, marking the best weekly performance since 2021, driven by foreign investor inflows and optimism around midterm results. The rally added approximately ₹28.7 lakh crore in market capitalization. Nifty reclaimed the 25,000 level as foreign institutional investors poured Rs 45,960 crore into Indian equities.

items.title: Anthropic IPO valuations tumble amid AI sell-off backlash
items.feedTitle: Anthropic IPO meets AI backlash after midterms show stinging rebuke of data centers
items.summary: Anthropic's planned IPO valuation has fallen from $1.5 trillion to $1.2–1.3 trillion range following the sharp correction in AI stocks and investor concerns over Democratic-backed regulations. The company proceeds despite market turbulence and declining investor enthusiasm for mega-cap AI funding rounds. Valuation pressures reflect broader skepticism about the sustainability of AI valuations.

items.title: US adds 165,000 jobs in October, beating forecasts
items.feedTitle: US job growth exceeds expectations in October despite economic uncertainty
items.summary: US employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, exceeding analyst expectations, with prior months' figures revised upward by a combined 84,000 positions. The resilient labor market shows the 'low-hire, low-fire' pattern persists amid economic uncertainty and geopolitical risks. An interest rate increase is expected in December as the Fed weighs inflation and employment trends.

finance.note: Oil prices remained under pressure as concerns over AI investment demand and slowing economic growth offset geopolitical risk premiums from Iran tensions. US stocks erased early post-midterm gains after a $2.5 trillion AI selloff, with the S&P 500 posting its worst week since April 2025, though Indian equities surged 8.5% as foreign investors rotated into emerging markets. Watch: earnings guidance revisions from mega-cap tech firms, Fed commentary on rate cuts, and energy demand signals from China.

cards.title: Context-switching cost is real
cards.insight: Every time you shift between tasks, your brain must reload context—email, Slack, document tabs. Research shows the average worker loses 23 minutes per interruption just regaining focus. The loss compounds: four interruptions equal 90+ minutes of wasted cognitive capacity.
cards.takeaway: Batch communication (check email and chat twice daily, not continuously) and use 90-minute focus blocks with phone on silent and notifications muted.

cards.title: Decision fatigue kills afternoons
cards.insight: Your mental energy for decisions depletes over the day, like a battery draining. Mornings carry 3–4x more decision quality than late afternoons. Delaying non-urgent choices to tomorrow—not evening—preserves focus for deep work now.
cards.takeaway: Schedule complex thinking and creative work before noon; save routine tasks and admin for afternoon slots.

cards.title: Boredom is a feature, not a bug
cards.insight: Cognitive science shows that mild boredom during breaks (not scrolling, not podcasts) allows the default-mode network to activate, consolidating learning and generating novel connections. Constant stimulation prevents this restorative phase.
cards.takeaway: Take 5–10 minute breaks with eyes closed or looking out a window—no phone—between focus sessions; this passive recovery boosts next-session performance.

cards.title: Specificity beats motivation
cards.insight: Willpower and motivation fluctuate; systems don't. A specific trigger ('After coffee, open code file X') and environment (same desk, same time) override the need to psych yourself up. Habit stacks motivation on autopilot.
cards.takeaway: Link your most important task to a consistent daily anchor (meal, commute end, etc.) and protect that time block like a meeting—make it boring and automatic.

The achievement showcases rapid progress in AI model capabilities for scientific problem-solving. The development highlights Anthropic's advances in AI-assisted research and reasoning.

ai.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion at $1.25 trillion valuation
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI raises $11 billion at $1.25 trillion valuation, falls short of $30 billion target
ai.summary: OpenAI closed a funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, raising $11 billion but falling short of its initial $1.4–$1.5 trillion target, according to reports. The shortfall reflects investor caution following the AI stock selloff. CEO Sam Altman's company maintains strong enterprise traction but faces valuation headwinds amid broader market skepticism.

ai.title: Democrats plan AI regulation targeting model safety expansion
ai.feedTitle: Democrats Plan Legislation for Artificial Intelligence
ai.summary: Incoming Democratic Congress majorities are preparing new legislation to expand AI oversight, particularly targeting model safety and rapid expansion practices (proposed, not final). The legislative push reflects voter concerns over data center impacts and AI safety. Bills likely to focus on environmental standards, safety benchmarks, and disclosure requirements for large-scale AI deployments.
